key_insight: The EHR-integrated GenAI tool (iHGR) identified inpatient VTE risk more sensitively than checklist-based order sets and slightly better than clinician judgment, while maintaining moderate specificity.
clinical_relevance: This suggests GenAI could help improve risk-appropriate thromboprophylaxis decisions in hospitals, especially where routine VTE risk stratification is inconsistent.
method: Multisite retrospective validation at Johns Hopkins Medicine using 500 randomly sampled adult inpatient admissions.
Compared iHGR and clinician-selected order set classifications against physician-adjudicated chart review as the reference standard.
Evaluated sensitivity, specificity, and error patterns across checklist-based and clinician judgment-based workflows.
evidence_signal: In the abstract, iHGR achieved 81.8% sensitivity and 70.9% specificity; the checklist-based order set had 61.3% sensitivity and 86.2% specificity, and the clinician judgment-based order set had 78.1% sensitivity and 65.4% specificity.
watch_item: False negatives were linked to missed narrative risk factors, highlighting the need for careful clinical data abstraction and human oversight before wider deployment.
paper_title: Multisite Real-World Validation of an Electronic Health Record-Integrated Generative Artificial Intelligence Tool for Venous Thromboembolism Risk Stratification
